privacy.notes: Synthetic Swift binding contract. It describes request and response structs, concrete file and CLI transport adapters, diagnostics, provenance, errors, fixture gates, and module readiness without committing calculator logic or licensed payloads.

public_calculator_contract.notes: The Swift binding request and response structs mirror the public calculator contract fields and only add transport metadata for file-exchange, CLI, service, and C ABI modes.

transport_modes.notes: Inspectible Parquet/CSV file-exchange primary path for offline and batch workflows consumed from Swift Foundation decoders.
Process-bound primary path for zero-build integration from Swift scripts and CLI tools via Foundation Process.
Fallback path for callers that need online request/response behavior via URLSession.
Future native path via C ABI using a Rust cdylib and Swift module map; not a current Swift support claim.

fields.name: pricing_year

fields.name: output_schema_version

fields.name: input_path

fields.name: output_path

fields.name: service_url
fields.notes: Configured service endpoint for the fallback transport path.

fields.name: correlation_id

fields.name: metadata

fields.name: fixture_gate

request_structs.notes: Single versioned Swift request envelope that mirrors the public calculator contract and adds only transport metadata.

response_structs.name: SwiftBindingResponse

fields.name: schema_version
fields.notes: Binding schema version for the response envelope.

fields.name: calculator_id
fields.notes: Echoes the public calculator identifier.

fields.name: pricing_year
fields.notes: Echoes the pricing year used during execution.

fields.name: mode
fields.notes: Declares the transport path that produced the result.

fields.name: success
fields.notes: True only when the request completed without a blocking error.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Machine-readable execution state for the caller.

fields.name: message
fields.notes: Short human-readable summary of the result.

fields.name: warnings
fields.notes: Non-blocking warnings attached to the response.

fields.name: errors
fields.notes: Machine-readable error records emitted when the response does not succeed.

fields.name: diagnostics
fields.notes: Structured diagnostic record with pass, fail, and blocked checks.

fields.name: provenance
fields.notes: Provenance record for the request and any generated artifact.

fields.name: service_url
fields.notes: Service endpoint used to complete the request.

fields.name: output_path
fields.notes: Output path used by the file boundary.

fields.name: fixture_gate_state
fields.notes: Observed fixture-gate outcome for the request.

fields.name: module_readiness_state
fields.notes: Observed Swift module readiness state for the binding bundle.

response_structs.notes: Single versioned Swift response envelope that captures success, diagnostics, provenance, and transport-specific outputs.

diagnostics.notes: The Swift request and response structs mirror the public calculator contract fields.
File-exchange and CLI invocation are the primary transport boundaries for Swift consumers.
Service fallback is explicitly declared for online request/response callers.
C ABI integration is a future native support gate and not a current Swift support claim.
Fixture gates remain synthetic-only or local-only and do not expose restricted payloads.
Module readiness distinguishes concrete file/CLI transport adapters from deferred service, C ABI, and publication gates.

provenance.notes: Name of the contract or validation command that produced the artifact.
Stable identifier for the Swift binding contract bundle.
Path to the source manifest or fixture record used to derive the example.
Public source URL or local reference used for provenance.
Retrieval date in ISO-8601 date form.
Checksum algorithm used by the bundle.

errors.condition: request or response fields do not match the published Swift binding schema
errors.notes: Use this when the envelope is structurally invalid.

errors.condition: the fallback service boundary cannot be reached
errors.notes: The caller may retry or switch to a file-exchange or CLI boundary.

errors.condition: CLI execution fails after a valid request
errors.notes: The failure is transport-level, not calculator logic.

errors.condition: File-exchange handoff cannot be read or written
errors.notes: Use for file-boundary errors in batch or offline handoff.

errors.condition: synthetic-only or local-only fixture gate is not satisfied
errors.notes: The request must stop before any restricted payload is handled.

errors.condition: the Swift adapter is unavailable or package promotion is deferred
errors.notes: Use this when local transport-boundary code is not available, or when a caller asks for Swift package publication evidence that is not claimed.

fixture_gates.notes: Committed examples must stay synthetic and metadata only.
Any licensed payloads stay local-only and user-supplied outside the repository.
The binding must remain pinned to the public calculator contract field set.

module_readiness.notes: The Swift package contains concrete request/response envelopes, file-boundary validation, and a CLI process adapter without claiming Swift Package Index publication.
The file-exchange boundary validates inspectable local input and output paths before handoff.
CLI invocation is implemented as a Foundation Process adapter that calls the shared command surface.
C ABI integration is documented as a future path and requires a Rust cdylib and Swift module map.

rules: Keep all examples synthetic and metadata only.
Mirror the public calculator contract fields explicitly.
Do not duplicate calculator math, thresholds, or adjustment logic in the Swift binding.
Prefer file-exchange or CLI first and use the service boundary when online request/response behavior is needed.
Keep diagnostics, provenance, and errors explicit and machine readable.
Keep fixture gates local-only and user-supplied for any licensed assets.
Keep the Swift package transport-only: file-boundary validation and CLI process invocation are allowed, calculator implementation is not.
C ABI integration remains a future native support gate, not a current Swift support claim.
